context: Tests whether the agent recognises URLs that defuddle cannot handle and picks a suitable alternative.

checklist.name: Identified the SPA limitation
checklist.description: The plan states that defuddle cannot execute JavaScript, so a client-rendered single-page app shell would return little or no content.

checklist.name: Chose WebFetch or informed the user for the SPA
checklist.description: The plan routes the SPA URL to WebFetch or tells the user the content cannot be extracted by defuddle, rather than running defuddle on it as if it were a normal article.

checklist.name: Identified the JSON endpoint as non-HTML
checklist.description: The plan states that the API URL returns JSON rather than an HTML page, so defuddle is the wrong tool.

checklist.name: Chose a direct fetch for the JSON endpoint
checklist.description: The plan uses a direct fetch (or tells the user it needs one) for the JSON endpoint instead of defuddle.

checklist.name: Did not run defuddle on the SPA without caveat
checklist.description: The agent did not run `defuddle parse` on the SPA URL as if success were guaranteed, or noted the empty-output risk if it tried.

checklist.name: Did not run defuddle on the JSON URL
checklist.description: The agent did not run `defuddle parse` against the JSON API endpoint.

checklist.name: Mentions the fallback rule
checklist.description: The plan mentions falling back to WebFetch when defuddle output is empty or navigation-only.

checklist.name: Explains the reasoning for each URL
checklist.description: Each URL has its own short reason tied to what defuddle does (server-side HTML stripping, no JavaScript, no credentials).

checklist.name: Produces plan.md
checklist.description: A file named `plan.md` exists in the working directory and addresses both URLs.

checklist.name: Does not recommend defuddle as the default for both
checklist.description: The plan does not claim defuddle is the best tool for both URLs.
